newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom NZ says Q3 earnings stable without PacStar.
newsitem.headline: Telecom NZ says Q3 earnings stable without PacStar.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand on Tuesday reported a 1.5 percent rise in net profit for the nine months to December 31, to NZ$528.1 million.
However, net profit for the third quarter slipped 8.2 percent to NZ$167.2 million when compared with the same period a year ago.
Telecom announced a third quarter dividend of 9.5 cents per share, against 8.5 cps last year.
Revenue for the nine months was $2.51 billion, up from 2.34 billion in the previous comparable period.
Telecom said that excluding Australian subsidiary Pacific Star, third quarter earnings were stable at $184.5 million.

It said that if the costs related to start up businesses Xtra and First Media were excluded in addition to the costs of Pacific Star, core earnings grew by 9.9 percent for the nine months and 4.1 percent for the three months.

"While volumes have continued to grow strongly, Telecom has reduced prices and faced the impact of a slower economy. These influences, coupled with volume and restructuring-driven cost increases, have meant a slowing in the rate of revenue growth," Telecom said.
